42862278.label: Background
42862278.text: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity significantly impacts the survival and quality of life of lymphoma patients. Since traditional echocardiographic markers often detect injury only after irreversible damage, there is an urgent need for early biomarkers. We aimed to evaluate the predictive value of myocardial FDG uptake patterns and quantitative parameters from routine oncologic PET/CT for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD).

42862278.label: Methods
42862278.text: This retrospective cohort study included lymphoma patients treated with anthracycline-based regimens at a single hospital between 2015 and 2024. Patients underwent FDG PET/CT at baseline and after chemotherapy. CTRCD was operationally defined using the LVEF-based component of the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guidelines on follow-up echocardiography. Metabolic parameters including maximal standard uptake value (SUVmax), cardiac metabolic volume (CMV), cardiac metabolic activity (CMA), and visual uptake patterns were analyzed on pre and post-treatment PET scans.

42862278.label: Results
42862278.text: Post-treatment SUVmax, CMV, and CMA were significantly higher in patients who developed cardiotoxicity (p = 0.04, 0.017, and 0.03, respectively). In univariable logistic regression, focal/diffuse myocardial uptake was significantly associated with CTRCD, whereas SUVmax ≥8.49 and CMV ≥66.9 showed borderline associations. In multivariable analysis including SUVmax, CMV, and focal/diffuse uptake pattern, only the focal/diffuse uptake pattern remained independently associated with CTRCD (OR = 10.71, 95% CI: 2.10-54.69, p = 0.004). Notably, absent myocardial FDG uptake after treatment was observed only in patients without CTRCD in this cohort. Baseline PET parameters showed no significant predictive value (p = n.s.).

42862278.label: Conclusion
42862278.text: Routine post-treatment oncologic FDG PET/CT may provide exploratory information on myocardial metabolic changes associated with CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Although quantitative PET parameters differed between patients with and without CTRCD, the focal/diffuse myocardial uptake pattern was the only imaging variable that remained independently associated with CTRCD after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation using standardized myocardial metabolic preparation and predefined imaging timepoints.

42864228.text: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

42914178.text: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

42957078.label: Background
42957078.text: Prior analyses of National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding to radiology departments have characterized aggregate grant volume and funding levels but have not systematically examined the institutional landscape of clinician-led research. This study characterized the institutional distribution of NIH funding awarded to clinician principal investigators (PIs) in diagnostic radiology (DR), interventional radiology (IR), and radiation oncology (RO) from fiscal years 2012 through 2025.

42957078.label: Methods
42957078.text: In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis, grant records were extracted from the NIH Research Portfolio Online Reporting Tools Expenditures and Results (RePORTER) database and filtered to PIs with an institutional department designation of "Radiation-Diagnostic/Oncology." Clinician investigators were identified by cross-referencing with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) datasets. Institutional funding, grant counts, unique investigators, grant mechanism portfolios, and career development awards were analyzed.

42957078.label: Results
42957078.text: A total of 437 unique clinician investigators (DR: 226; IR: 46; RO: 165) were identified, accounting for $1.65 billion in inflation-adjusted funding. NIH-funded clinicians were distributed across 47 institutions in DR, 29 in IR, and 45 in RO. The top five institutions accounted for 34.5% of grants and 38.4% of total funding, largely reflecting workforce size: institutional clinician PI count explained 82% of the variance in funding, and funding per clinician PI was more evenly distributed (Gini 0.38) than total funding (Gini 0.62). Stanford received the largest grant funding in DR ($134.9M), UC San Francisco in IR ($36.9M), and University of Michigan in RO ($68.1M). R01 awards were the dominant mechanism across all subspecialties. Forty new K-awards were issued across 21 institutions.

42957078.label: Conclusions
42957078.text: NIH funding to radiology clinician investigators is concentrated at a small number of academic medical centers, principally because those centers host larger clinician investigator workforces, with a narrow clinician-scientist pipeline. These findings identify opportunities to broaden research capacity across the radiology workforce.

42962778.label: Objective
42962778.text: To characterize event-to-payment or report-processing latency among physicians with imaging-related allegations.

42962778.label: Methods
42962778.text: This retrospective cross-sectional study included National Practitioner Data Bank physician payment reports processed from 2004 to 2025, excluding state-fund reports. Imaging-related allegations were identified using a specific-allegation field. Latency equaled the original report-processing year minus the alleged-event end year, using the onset year when the end year was unavailable. Adjusted models included report characteristics and jurisdiction, with practitioner-clustered standard errors. Complementary analyses examined events from 2004 to 2010 and jurisdiction random effects.

42962778.label: Results
42962778.text: Among 199,060 eligible reports, 1,980 involved imaging-related allegations (1,852 physicians). The median latency was 4 y (interquartile range, 3-6); 47.0% had a latency of ≥5 y. The proportions were 43.7% (2004-2009), 42.9% (2010-2015), 46.1% (2016-2020), and 55.7% (2021-2025). Adjusted differences were +0.66 y for permanent injury and +0.48 for death versus nonpermanent injury, +0.38 for outpatient and +0.49 for mixed settings versus inpatient care, and +1.56 for judgment versus settlement or other. All corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) excluded 0. Age was associated with -0.16 y per decade-category increment. Among 562 reports for events from 2004 to 2010, the median latency was 4 y, and 44.1% had a latency of ≥5 y. The adjusted payment ratio per additional latency year was 1.021 (95% confidence interval, 0.997-1.044; P = 0.082).

42962778.label: Discussion
42962778.text: Paid reports involving physicians with imaging-related allegations frequently reflected care delivered years earlier. The payment association was small, imprecise, and not statistically significant. These selected paid-report data do not estimate litigation duration, future payment risk, or radiologist-specific performance.

42998628.label: Background
42998628.text: Positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive whole-body assessment of molecular biomarkers and is particularly valuable for evaluating heterogeneous diseases such as cancer. Platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (PDGFRβ) is a stromal biomarker expressed on activated pericytes and fibroblasts that contributes to tumour remodelling, vascular regulation and therapeutic resistance. This study describes the translational implementation of the PDGFRβ-targeting PET tracer [68Ga]Ga-ATH001, from GMP-compliant radiopharmaceutical development to its first reported oncology application in patients with liver tumours.

42998628.label: Methods
42998628.text: A GMP-compliant automated synthesis of [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 was established using a ModularLab PharmTracer synthesizer and validated for clinical use. The tracer was prospectively implemented in the IMAGINE-1 study (EU CT 2025-522290-11-00). PET imaging included dynamic liver acquisition immediately after injection, followed by whole-body PET/CT imaging and delayed liver scans to assess tracer biodistribution, tumour uptake and tracer kinetics.

42998628.label: Results
42998628.text: [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 was successfully translated into clinical production using an automated in-house synthesis process, achieving a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 51.9 ± 0.7 %, radiochemical purity of 97 %, radiochemical stability of 96.3 ± 0.5 % after 2 h at room temperature and apparent molar activity of 47.2 ± 1.6 GBq/µmol at EOS. Three consecutive production runs assessed reproducibility; a fourth batch served as a microbiological worst-case challenge and was excluded from the assessment. PET/CT imaging in three patients with colorectal liver metastases showed SUVpeak tumour-to-background ratios of 1.5 to 1.8 at 60 min after injection.

42998628.label: Conclusion
42998628.text: GMP-compliant production enabled the first reported oncology application of [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 in patients with liver tumours. The ongoing phase 1 IMAGINE-1 study will further evaluate its clinical potential.

42998628.label: Eu trial registration
42998628.text: Clinical Trials Information system: CTIS, EU CT 2025-522290-11-00, Registered 29 September 2025, IMAGINE-1 | 2025-522290-11-00 | CTIS.eu.

43019228.text: An 11-year-old girl with neuroblastoma, enrolled in a clinical trial, underwent 18F-MFBG PET/CT for treatment response evaluation. Imaging showed multiple metastatic lesions. Focal increased radiotracer uptake was also seen in the uterus. Menstrual history confirmed active menstruation, and pelvic ultrasound showed normal uterine morphology and echotexture. This case demonstrates that physiological uterine 18F-MFBG uptake can occur during menstruation-a benign phenomenon that must be recognized to avoid false-positive interpretation of PET/CT findings.

43019578.text: A 55-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of drug-resistant epilepsy with monthly clinical seizures. Investigation revealed a left frontoethmoidal nasal meningoencephalocele secondary to osseous fibrous dysplasia. Video-EEG failed to capture scalp epileptiform activity, but a concomitant intranasal electrode recorded frequent, clinically silent electrographic seizures. This continuous intranasal EEG recording during the uptake phase of 18F-FDG PET/CT confirmed eight localized subclinical seizures, each lasting 1-3 minutes. The PET scan demonstrated intense focal hypermetabolism at the herniated tissue tip, matching the electrographic EEG ictal activity. Complete endoscopic endonasal lesionectomy rendered the patient seizure-free for 4 years.

43055828.label: Objectives
43055828.text: To evaluate diagnostic performance, radiation dose, and quantitative spectral characteristics of dual-phase photon-counting CT (PCD-CT) for parathyroid adenoma localization after inconclusive first-line imaging.

43055828.label: Materials and methods
43055828.text: Consecutive patients with primary hyperparathyroidism and negative, discordant, or inconclusive first-line imaging underwent paired [18F]FECh PET/CT and dual-phase PCD-CT with arterial and venous acquisitions. Three radiologists, blinded to clinical and reference-standard information, retrospectively assessed arterial and portal-venous 40- and 70-keV images and VNC reconstructions. The reference standard comprised surgery/histopathology with biochemical confirmation, concordant PET/CT with persistent biochemical disease in nonsurgical positive patients, or clinical/biochemical resolution in negative patients. Lesion-level sensitivity, positive predictive value (PPV), and interreader intraclass correlation (ICC) were calculated. Aorta-normalized attenuation and wash-in and wash-out metrics were compared among adenomas, thyroid tissue, and lymph nodes.

43055828.label: Results
43055828.text: Forty-nine patients (mean age, 64.2 ± 10.9 years; 42 women) were included, with 45 patients having 49 reference-standard-positive lesions. PCD-CT lesion-level sensitivity was 67.3%-83.7%, and PPV 67.3%-90.0%, with an interreader agreement of 0.506. Aorta-adjusted wash-out was greater in adenomas (27.2%) than in thyroid (20.2%) and lymph nodes (-3.1%; both p < 0.001). Arterial adenoma-thyroid attenuation and wash-in overlapped between adenomas did not differ significantly (arterial p = 0.615 and thyroid tissue. 0.945 at 40 and 70 keV; wash-in p = 0.363). Mean estimated effective dose was 1.23 ± 0.47 mSv.

43055828.label: Conclusion
43055828.text: Dual-phase PCD-CT provided reader-dependent parathyroid localization at low radiation dose in a difficult second-line cohort. Quantitative wash-out may aid differentiation from thyroid and lymph-node mimics but requires prospective threshold validation.

43055828.label: Key points
43055828.text: Question Inconclusive first-line imaging complicates parathyroid lesion localization. Findings Reader sensitivity ranged from 67.3% to 83.7% at 1.23 mSv. Critical relevance statement Aorta-adjusted wash-out differed among parathyroid lesions, thyroid tissue, and lymph nodes.

43057878.text: Dynamic 18F-FDG PET enables brain kinetic quantification to study central nervous system involvement in cancer and other systemic diseases, but reliable blood input functions are difficult to obtain on conventional scanners. We used total-body PET to evaluate 18F-FDG kinetic modeling of the brain in healthy subjects and patients with genitourinary cancer (GUC). Methods: Ten patients with GUC and 12 healthy participants underwent a 1-h total-body 18F-FDG dynamic scan, and image-derived input functions were extracted from the aorta. Reversible and irreversible 2-tissue compartment (2Tr and 2Ti, respectively) models were assessed in the gray matter, thalamus, putamen, and brainstem using Akaike information criterion. Microparameters (K 1, k 2, k 3), net influx rate (K i), and practical model identifiability were assessed, and differences between patients with GUC and healthy participants were investigated. Results: The 2Tr model provided significantly better fits than the 2Ti model (P < 0.05). K i and SUV were significantly lower in patients with GUC across multiple brain regions. The 2Tr model revealed significant differences in K 1, k 2, and k 3 between the cohorts, independent of age, which were absent or attenuated when the 2Ti model was used. Identifiability analysis confirmed robust parameter estimation with reasonable bias and SD. Conclusion: Total-body dynamic PET enabled robust, noninvasive quantification of brain 18F-FDG kinetics using an image-derived input function. The 2Tr model provided superior time-activity curve fitting and identifiable parameters and revealed group differences in microparameters (K 1 and k 2) that were not detected with the 2Ti model. These findings suggest alterations in brain metabolism in patients with GUC, warranting further investigation.

43064878.label: Objective
43064878.text: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.

43064878.label: Materials and methods
43064878.text: This multicenter retrospective study included 592 patients with PDAC who underwent R0 surgical resection. A Swin Transformer-assisted DL classifier (Outcome Prediction for PDAC, OP-PDAC) was built using multi-planar contrast-enhanced CT scans (axial, coronal, and sagittal planes). Radiogenomic analysis was conducted in 41 patients to elucidate the biological underpinnings of the OP-PDAC. Furthermore, the Intelligent Prognosis Stratification System (IPSS-PDAC) was developed by incorporating clinicopathological variables into the OP-PDAC framework.

43064878.label: Results
43064878.text: In the derivation and test cohorts, the C‑index of OP-PDAC for predicting 1‑year disease‑free survival (DFS) ranged from 0.807 to 0.844, which was significantly higher than that of the clinicopathological model (CP-PDAC; C‑index, 0.631-0.656). The IPSS-PDAC further enhanced predictive performance, yielding a C‑index of 0.836-0.871, and enabled effective stratification for both DFS and overall survival (all log‑rank p < 0.01). Radiogenomic analysis revealed that high‑risk patients exhibited an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, elevated stromal scores, activated oncogenic pathways, and reduced CD8+ T‑cell infiltration.

43064878.label: Conclusion
43064878.text: IPSS-PDAC is a non-invasive and robust prognostic stratification system that integrates imaging features and clinicopathological features. By sensitively reflecting tumor heterogeneity and TME, it provides references for clinical decision-making in the postoperative management of PDAC patients.

43064878.label: Key points
43064878.text: Question This study constructs an integrated prognostic model combining imaging signatures and guideline-recommended clinicopathological variables to address unmet clinical challenges in postoperative risk stratification for PDAC patients. Findings A multi-planar Swin Transformer-based deep learning model (IPSS-PDAC) achieves a C-index of 0.836-0.871 for disease-free survival prediction. Critical relevance statement High-risk patients stratified by the OP-PDAC model display a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, activation of core oncogenic signaling pathways, and reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration.

43071178.label: Purpose
43071178.text: Structural MRI and 18F-FDG PET are clinically established imaging biomarkers of neuronal injury in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Synaptic density PET (SV2A), arterial spin labelling (ASL, perfusion), and cortical thickness (CTh) can offer additional information, but have not been compared within the same patients. We performed a head-to-head evaluation of these imaging measures for detecting neurodegeneration, discriminating AD from healthy volunteers (HV) and examining their associations with cognition.

43071178.label: Methods
43071178.text: Thirty-six biomarker-confirmed AD patients (71 ± 9 y/o; M/F 17/19) underwent 18F-FDG, 18F-SynVesT-1 PET/MR and neuropsychological evaluation. Patients were classified as MCI-stage (CDR = 0.5, n = 22) or dementia-stage (CDR > 0.5, n = 14). Image processing and analysis was performed in CAT12.9 with partial volume correction for PET. PET and ASL measures were normalized to the whole cerebellum. Classification performance was evaluated with partial least squares discriminant analysis and Firth logistic regression under repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

43071178.label: Results
43071178.text: In the MCI-stage, reductions were mainly found in the temporal cortex. In the dementia-stage, reductions for the 5 imaging measures extended to the temporoparietal, precuneal and frontal cortices. 18F-FDG PET, assessed against a separate HV cohort, showed large reductions (Cohen's d up to -2.5) and excellent discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.94). Among the cortical measures evaluated against the same HV, cortical thickness showed the largest reductions (d up to -1.6). Cortical thickness, 18F-SynVesT-1 and volumetry provided similar discriminatory performance (AUC 0.81-0.86). ASL did not show detectable reductions in MCI and had a lower AUC (0.72). Global cognition was associated with widespread atrophy, cortical thinning, and 18F-FDG hypometabolism, whereas domain-specific cognitive measures showed more localized regional associations. 18F-SynVesT-1 and ASL demonstrated weaker and less consistent correlations.

43071178.label: Conclusion
43071178.text: Multimodal PET and MRI measures showed overlapping yet distinct spatial patterns of neurodegeneration. In MCI, structural, metabolic and synaptic abnormalities were found, whereas perfusion deficits only significantly emerged in dementia-stage AD. Structural and functional measures differentially relate to global and domain-specific cognitive decline. The study was registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05384353) as of 20 May 2022.
